scope: Concept image generation and targeted visual revisions; no Blender work

content.intent: revise industrial starting point into concept sketch master
content.prompt:
Use case: style-transfer.
Asset type: MASTER HAND-DRAWN CONCEPT SHEET for one original human space-ark carrier GUIHANG. Image 1 is the existing rough design to revise, not a finished ship.
User direction: grounded Mobile Suit Gundam-style naval mechanical design, restrained and handsome, no fantasy monument. FIRST CONCEPT SKETCHES, not Blender renders or final manufacturing drawings.
Revise these specific design weaknesses in the reference:
1. Keep its heavy enclosed long body, short faceted bow, warm-white / slate-blue / graphite / sparse brick-red palette. Replace the monotonous cargo-box profile with THREE clear connected masses: thick protected forward shoulder, slightly recessed midship service waist, broad aft engineering shoulders. These are substantial hull transitions, not wings or added spikes.
2. Make the command bridge a LOW compact semi-recessed armored island in the aft third. Remove the tall forest of naval antenna masts and the giant row of bridge windows. The ship is kilometer-class; fine grouped inhabited window lights must be tiny. Keep one short sensor mast.
3. On the visible PORT side of the midship service waist, clearly show TWO distinct rectangular recessed mouths side by side along the hull length, separated by a thick structural pier. The FORWARD mouth is LAUNCH; the AFT mouth is RECOVERY, a little wider. Actual dark tunnel depth, outer doors, inner framing and guides visible in BOTH mouths. These are side-facing, safely ahead of the stern thrusters. A tiny original humanoid mobile-frame in the launch cradle and a tiny four-arm industrial frame near the recovery mouth identify the carrier's role. No generic shuttle as the only payload.
4. The stern has SIX main engine apertures TOTAL, arranged as TWO columns of THREE, clearly built into sturdy structural modules. Fore-aft direction obvious. From the hero view only the near bank and part of the far bank need be visible. Small attitude thrusters and short cooling vanes; not giant fins.
5. Preserve a broad quiet sealed forebody for sleeping community, a thin grouped habitation band above the waist, dense service details only around the two ports, and separately colored aft machinery. A few replaced panels and dark sealed sectors imply a long life; no luxurious terraces or exposed parks.
Layout 1536x1024 landscape, tasteful HAND-DRAWN DESIGN SKETCH presentation on off-white paper. Top 70 percent: one complete revised mother ship in front-port three-quarter view, enough side visible to read both ports, generous margins. Bottom left 25 percent: small strict SIDE silhouette sketch of the SAME ship, showing the low bridge and three mass transitions. Bottom right 25 percent: enlarged mechanical detail of the SAME paired side ports with central divider, 20-meter-class mecha dwarfed by the doorway, thick opening rim and inner rail/capture frame. Labels ONLY "GUIHANG / CARRIER STUDY", "LAUNCH", "RECOVERY" in small restrained drafting typography. No fake handwritten paragraphs, no dimensions, no second ship alternative.
Style: professional original anime-mecha designer's exploratory pen/pencil and marker sheet, clean purposeful contour lines with subtle construction lines, restrained color blocking, crisp shaded angular surfaces, legible dark mechanical recesses. Beauty through proportions and controlled detail. NOT a photograph, CGI product render, stone building, rounded seed, crown, scythe, luxury liner or toy. Do not copy Archangel's split prow, any Gundam logo or any existing franchise ship. No gun batteries, space background, planets or bright engine bloom. This is a concept mother sheet, not a validated technical projection.

Use case: precise-object-edit.
Image 1 is the edit target, a hand-drawn master sheet for the original GUIHANG mother ship. Retain the main ship's silhouette, materials, color placement, camera, page layout, title, three-level stern engine bank and low bridge. Make ONLY a coordinated drawing-consistency correction:
A. The lower-left side-view inset incorrectly lacks the two visible PORT side openings. Replace that small inset with a true PORT side elevation of the SAME hero ship: short angled bow, same low bridge position, same armored midship waist containing TWO rectangular mouths separated by the same broad vertical pier, forward mouth launch and aft mouth recovery. Same height and fore-aft positions relative to the body as the hero. Do not label the incorrect old drawing as another side.
B. In BOTH main hero and bottom-right port-detail inset, replace the recognizable colorful humanoid with a tiny neutral grey industrial humanoid scale placeholder and the industrial machine with a comparably small grey 4-arm placeholder. Their height must be about ONE FIFTH of each LARGE exterior service-bay aperture, NOT half. Preserve exactly the same relative size in hero and detail. Large exterior service alcoves are not themselves human-sized airlocks.
C. Deep inside each of these large exterior service mouths, clearly indicate a smaller framed machine transit throat, a supported guide/capture cradle and a visible heavy sliding panel parked in a side pocket. The vehicle remains about half the smaller inner transit throat's height. Use simple modular parallel guide structures, not a busy factory maze. The space between the paired mouths remains solid, structural and consistent in all views. The labels LAUNCH and RECOVERY remain attached to the correct corresponding mouths.
D. Keep the underlying drawing restrained and hand-drafted, with graphite and marker shading on warm paper; no dimension numbers, no invented diagrams, no additional vessels or labels, no change to the rest of the ship.
This is visual concept coherence, not engineering certification. Make the same object repeat faithfully across the sheet.

Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: HAND-DRAWN CONCEPT MASTER for three original shipborne machine roles belonging to the human ark GUIHANG, not a finished game render.
Make one coherent professional Japanese mecha design sheet on ivory drafting paper, 1536x1024 landscape, three clear columns with full-body three-quarter drawings and generous margins. Precise pencil/ink contour, subtle construction lines, restrained marker colors, lively yet legible mechanical design. Main palette shared with mother ship: warm-white armor, slate blue-gray frame, dark graphite flexible depths, sparse brick-red identity panels and amber service catches. Tiny neutral human scale silhouettes, no exact dimensions or fake technical paragraphs. Labels only EXPLORER / SENTINEL / HARVESTER.
LEFT EXPLORER: non-humanoid compact observation machine. Low flat sensory torso, one recessed horizontal optical sensor bar, two articulated survey outriggers with dish/antenna ends, two compact sampling claws under the body, tiny vectoring thrust pods, short docking skids. No conventional airplane nose or wings, no full human legs, no cartoon face. Frame can fold into a small serviced package. Delicate and precise, clear instrument modules, no gun.
CENTER SENTINEL: original 20-meter-class humanoid protective combat/work frame. Synthesize layered industrial mecha skeleton, elegant wrapping chest/forearm armor and role-specific maneuvering equipment into ONE original coherent design. Low flattened faceless sensor head recessed in a high protective collar, NO forehead horns or V-fin. Forward-wrapping rounded chest shell over mechanical rib cage, protective shoulder roots with visible elbow/knee mechanisms, balanced waist, strong but relatively agile legs, short broad feet. Two compact replaceable back-thruster pods, small calf nozzles; no huge wings. Left forearm has an angular tool-shield with a U-shaped rescue attachment recess and protected tow point. Right hand holds a simple short fictional carbine lowered; military equipment is understated. Do not use recognizable Gundam head/chest blocks, Tekkaman horns/crystals/lance, or an existing Mecha BREAK silhouette. Elegant armor coverage belongs to a serviceable machine, not a supernatural suit. No glowing magic core.
RIGHT HARVESTER: non-humanoid low broad industrial core, two thick front anchoring arms ending in padded rock clamps, plus two secondary articulated tool arms (one enclosed mechanical cutter, one material gripper), removable ore cassette seated in the aft chassis, short stabilizing grapples and compact maneuver thrusters. Exactly FOUR main arms with clear joints and routing, not a pile of random limbs. Dense mechanical effort at tools, quiet armored central volume; reads as a heavy work machine, not a tank or animal.
All three share paired rectangular capture lugs and a visibly standardized dorsal or ventral maintenance saddle, repeatable service access plates and attachment markings. Distinct silhouette and function even without labels. Small patches and worn grasp points imply work, never luxurious chrome. NO space scenery, portals, foliage, large guns, projectile detail, brands, franchise emblems, UI, photorealistic CGI or dimension claims. This is an art-development sketch plate, not a production drawing.

jobs.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Create an original HAND-DRAWN industrial mecha concept-development sheet on ivory drafting paper, 1536x1024 landscape. Match input image 1, the GUIHANG mother ship master, as the authoritative exterior visual identity. Warm-white armor, slate blue-gray structure, graphite recesses, sparse brick-red identification, amber work lights. Crisp pencil/ink contour, light construction lines, controlled marker shadows. No photoreal CGI, no fantasy monument, no generic new ship or copied franchise, no fake dimension numbers, no unreadable handwritten paragraphs. These are concept views, not validated engineering projections. Preserve low bridge aft of center, short faceted bow, thick enclosed body, TWO port-side midship mouths separated by one thick pier (forward LAUNCH, aft RECOVERY), six aft engine apertures total in two columns of three, only short fins. Small figures in the reference are schematic, not exact scale evidence.
Asset: coherent six-view concept sheet of this SAME ship, not six alternatives. Layout top two rows each with two long horizontal ship views; bottom row with two end views and generous blank margins. Labels only PORT, STARBOARD, TOP, BOTTOM, BOW, STERN.
PORT: bow left, stern right, BOTH rectangular side service mouths visibly open at the midship waist, bridge in same aft position and three visible near-bank nozzles.
STARBOARD: mirror longitudinal orientation with bow right, stern left; opposite side is plated service access with CLOSED rectangular maintenance panels, no invented open garden or symmetric active hangar.
TOP: bow left and stern right, one central longitudinal spine, paired shoulder masses, compact low bridge, near-side hangar recess corresponding to PORT. BOTTOM: bow left and stern right, reinforced keel and maintenance hatches; no bridge and no duplicated dorsal details.
BOW: short faceted nose facing directly toward viewer, broad shoulder silhouette behind it and tiny centered bridge silhouette above; NO engine holes at the nose.
STERN: directly behind, exactly SIX main nozzles as two vertical columns of THREE circles; structure between columns, tiny bridge above. Do not turn them into four or eight.
All views in restrained mostly orthographic drawing language, no extreme perspective, line weight separates primary silhouette from panel detail. Keep the same bow slope, hull beam, bridge location, port longitudinal position and engine count across ALL views. Fill the page elegantly without overlap. Do not add decorative inset shapes or extra views.

Match input image 1, the GUIHANG mother ship master, as the authoritative exterior visual identity. Warm-white armor, slate blue-gray structure, graphite recesses, sparse brick-red identification, amber work lights. Crisp pencil/ink contour, light construction lines, controlled marker shadows. Small figures in the reference are schematic, not exact scale evidence.
Asset: clear hull decomposition and internal zoning CONCEPT study for the SAME mother ship.
Upper 60 percent: three-quarter EXPLODED ASSEMBLY drawing of the vessel with its coherent graphite structural backbone continuous. Lift only the major warm-white external armor sections slightly away with dotted guide lines: forward protection/nose cap, preserved-community compartment shells, central dorsal cover, port hangar shoulder cover, aft power cover. Keep both launch/recovery mouths together as a single side assembly. Aft complete engine assembly remains SIX nozzles, two columns of three. Explosion is modest and readable, not a cloud of random parts. Inner functional modules are large architectural volumes, not fully engineered reactors.
Lower 40 percent: same ship in PORT-side longitudinal CUTAWAY, bow left stern right. Clearly separate seven zones in this order and with tiny English labels only: SHIELD at bow, PRESERVATION with isolated sleeping/seed compartments forward, HABITAT inside protected midbody, HANGAR on port side of that region, INDUSTRY aft of habitats, POWER well aft, DRIVE at stern.
HABITAT is an ENCLOSED rotating-drum candidate INSIDE the hull, longitudinal axis, located inward and toward starboard from the port hangar. Show its curved residential decks as an internal module, not an enormous ring sticking out of the exterior or a floating garden. Central service spine is nonrotating. Hangar side module occupies a DISTINCT volume, not drawn through the residential drum. Show a simple separation between life/preservation systems and aft power volume. Front preserved-community blocks have redundancy, not one fragile glowing crystal.
Keep the open twin side bays in the same place as the exterior and the bridge small. Use lightly differentiated muted tints for zones and solid simple structural interfaces. No energy magic, no giant fuel flames, no arbitrary rooms whose scale pretends to be validated. Show how the parts relate; no numerical measurements.

Use case: stylized-concept. Create an original HAND-DRAWN industrial mecha concept-development sheet on ivory drafting paper, 1536x1024 landscape. Match input image 1, the GUIHANG mother ship master, as the authoritative exterior visual identity. Warm-white armor, slate blue-gray structure, graphite recesses, sparse brick-red identification, amber work lights. Crisp pencil/ink contour, light construction lines, controlled marker shadows. No photoreal CGI, no fantasy monument, no generic new ship or copied franchise, no fake dimension numbers, no unreadable handwritten paragraphs. These are concept views, not validated engineering projections. Preserve low bridge aft of center, short faceted bow, thick enclosed body, TWO port-side midship mouths separated by one thick pier (forward LAUNCH, aft RECOVERY), six aft engine apertures total in two columns of three, only short fins. Small figures in the reference are schematic, not exact scale evidence.
Input image 2 defines ORIGINAL shipborne machines: small nonhumanoid EXPLORER, armored humanoid SENTINEL, four-arm HARVESTER. Match their form family.
Asset: a hand-drawn HANGAR and PORT OPERATIONS design sheet, NOT a new exterior design.
Upper left dominant 60 percent: interior perspective looking from the aft maintenance gallery toward the port-side hull with TWO separate exterior openings visible, forward LAUNCH and aft RECOVERY, separated by a thick fixed pier. Through each opening is dark space without a giant planet. Put the humanoid in a supported launch cradle by one lane; put a folded four-arm harvester in the separate capture/inspection area, not blocking the launch lane. Clearly show outer service alcove, smaller machine transit throat, inner doors and their side parking pockets. Rails and clamp arms have actual mounting points. The machine is large relative to a HUMAN worker, at least ten times their height; humans only inside small PRESSURIZED service boxes behind windows, or in visibly tethered pressure suits. No casual people standing in vacuum, no stools or houseplants in open hangar.
Bottom left: one very simple TOP-DOWN block layout. Exterior/space is to left, interior maintenance to right. Two parallel routes through two separate gates: outgoing LAUNCH arrow to left, incoming RECOVERY arrow to right. Capture and unload sit only on the incoming line; shared transfer gallery at rear has a clear stop point, not overlapping through-traffic. Do not point both arrows outwards.
Right column: exploded detail of ONE sliding port-door module: outer frame attached to hull, thick sliding leaf displaced into its adjacent recessed pocket, guide mechanism, inner fixed capture saddle with paired locks, and service umbilical kept disconnected until capture. Small second inset shows the same door CLOSED flush. Only minimal labels LAUNCH / RECOVERY / SERVICE / DOOR MODULE / CLOSED.
Lighting concentrated on clamps and active lanes; some service bays dark and sealed. Show pressure boundaries as thick glass and local small airlocks, not a giant repeatedly pressurized hangar. No blueprint dimension claims, no free-floating parts except explicit exploded inset.

Use case: stylized-concept. Create an original professional HAND-DRAWN CONCEPT sheet, 1536x1024 landscape, ivory paper, crisp pencil/ink, light construction lines, restrained colored markers. Same design family as the GUIHANG mother ship in input image 1: warm-white panels, blue-gray thick structure, graphite mechanical recesses, sparse brick-red identity blocks, local amber work lights, serviceable modular parts. No photoreal CGI, no generic luxury spacecraft, no random glowing holograms, no dimension claims, no dense fake text. This is concept development before Blender, not an engineering drawing.
Asset: the compact protected COMMAND BRIDGE inside the small aft command island of this exact ship. Upper 65 percent is one rich interior perspective from the rear looking forward. Six to eight functional workstations in a modest room, not an auditorium. Two forward navigation/port-control seats, four midroom operator consoles, one compact aft coordination desk. Small thick recessed observation windows, more emphasis on physical inset instrument panels and clean limited displays than giant panoramic glass. UI is abstract quiet blocks, no readable paragraphs. Rigid seat frames with lap/shoulder restraints, foot captures and grabrails make axial LOW-GRAVITY operation legible. Crew are seated and restrained or attached to rails, no free-standing coffee cups. Walk/handhold passages at both sides, two identifiable rear pressure doors and a maintenance access hatch. Warm light on faces, equipment lights subtle. One inactive station under a fabric cover, a tiny clipped personal photograph and an unfinished shift card give human history.
Bottom left: simple top-down PLAN of the SAME room with matching seat count, forward window strip, side passages and two aft doors.
Bottom right: exploded side-detail of ONE operator station in four visually connected layers: structural pedestal/foot restraint, seat frame and harness, cushioning, hinged control console and under-seat service connector; plus a tiny wall slice showing outside armor, pressure shell and inner equipment lining. Parts have dotted assembly lines; no invented zero-g chair floating without mounts.
Labels only BRIDGE / PLAN / OPERATOR STATION / PRESSURE SHELL. Preserve a restrained naval industrial mood; people are small and ordinary, no franchise uniforms or emblems.

Use case: stylized-concept. Create an original professional HAND-DRAWN CONCEPT sheet, 1536x1024 landscape, ivory paper, crisp pencil/ink, light construction lines, restrained colored markers. Same design family as the GUIHANG mother ship in input image 1: warm-white panels, blue-gray thick structure, graphite mechanical recesses, sparse brick-red identity blocks, local amber work lights, serviceable modular parts. No photoreal CGI, no generic luxury spacecraft, no random glowing holograms, no dimension claims, no dense fake text. This is concept development before Blender, not an engineering drawing.
Asset: a communal room inside the ark's enclosed ROTATING HABITAT candidate, intimate human life, not a luxury liner. Upper 65 percent: one human-eye-level interior perspective. A long narrow modular room with subtle curved deck and repeating structural ribs, eight seats around one shared table, seven simple meal settings, a food-service niche, storage wall and an ordinary sealed door leading to an unawakened residential sector. No huge exterior window: room is deep inside protected hull. Small porthole into another pressurized circulation corridor only. Lit active half uses warm white panels, worn composite tabletop, fabric acoustic pads and a few repaired cup straps; closed sector beyond the far door stays cool and quiet. Show two or three ordinary crew in maintenance clothes sharing work/food, no royalty, no magic technology. Trays and cups have modest anti-spill clips. A folded garment and a repaired textile sleeve make it feel like a lived-in home. Thin brick-red door identification panel, physically attached rail lights.
Bottom left: plain PLAN, eight-seat table in center, service niche and lockers along one wall, entry on one end and sealed sector door opposite. Plan must match main perspective rather than invent another room.
Bottom center: tiny section diagram showing the room on the INNER curved deck of an ENCLOSED rotating drum inside a nonrotating hull. Its floor's outward radial direction is clear. A central nonrotating service spine and a small controlled transfer vestibule are distinct; do not connect ordinary doors directly between incompatible rotating structures. This is a schematic conceptual relationship, not solved bearings.
Bottom right: exploded TABLE assembly with anchored serviceable base, replaceable slab, removable tray/cup clips, underside service-light rail, dotted assembly guides. No houseplants, decorative trees, chandeliers, glass city dome or balconies.
Labels only COMMON ROOM / PLAN / HABITAT SECTION / TABLE MODULE. Mood: a few people slowly bringing a vast ship back to life.

Use case: precise-object-edit. Derive a HAND-DRAWN mechanical concept sheet of the SENTINEL humanoid ONLY from the CENTER machine in input image 1. The reference contains three roles: do NOT redesign the explorer or harvester here. Preserve Sentinel's low flattened hornless head, amber visor recessed in high collar, broad wrapping chest shell and shoulder roots, exposed compact mechanical waist, thick shins, dark knees, short wide feet, warm-white/navy/graphite with sparse brick red. Its LEFT arm carries the same long tool-shield; RIGHT hand the same lowered fictional carbine. Original design, no new V-fin, crown, crystal or decorative wings.
Purpose: resolve the back-equipment ambiguity and explain parts, not a second armor variant.
1536x1024 ivory drawing paper, crisp ink/pencil with muted marker shading. Three main panels:
LEFT: clear full-body FRONT view of the exact same Sentinel, neutral stance, consistent armor shapes.
CENTER: full-body BACK view of the same Sentinel, showing exactly TWO main compact maneuvering pods mounted symmetrically high left and right. Between them is a clearly visible CENTRAL capture saddle, lower than the pod tops, with two mechanical locking lugs and an unobstructed approach path from behind. A protected service connector sits below the saddle. Do not fill that space with a third giant thruster or spine backpack.
RIGHT: exploded three-quarter arrangement of the SAME machine with armored torso shells and shoulder/shin plates displaced only a little from an unarmored mechanical skeleton, the TWO back pods displaced to the sides, central saddle and shield/carbine as separate attached-system parts, dotted guides back to mounting locations. Do not add extra arms or legs, duplicate head or turn the skeleton into a human.
Small lower-right inset: closer saddle/paired locks and disconnected service plug, showing plug attaches only after mechanical capture. Number ONLY four back elements consistently across back and exploded drawings: 1 left pod, 2 right pod, 3 central saddle, 4 service plug. Labels only FRONT / BACK / SYSTEM BREAKDOWN / CAPTURE INTERFACE. No fake dimension text. Keep upper armor silhouette coherent across all three panels; left and right are the machine's own sides. This is a concept assembly, not validated engineering, rigging or weapon construction.

Use case: precise-object-edit. Derive an ORIGINAL HAND-DRAWN mechanical assembly study from the LEFT EXPLORER and RIGHT HARVESTER in input image 1, preserving their identity. Do not include the humanoid center machine. 1536x1024 ivory drafting paper, pencil/ink and quiet colored marker, warm-white armor, slate blue-gray structure, graphite joints, brick-red identity patches, amber tool warnings. Make two generous columns.
LEFT EXPLORER: show its compact horizontal optical-black sensor face, two articulated sensing outriggers, two sampling claws and short docking skids in a large three-quarter EXPLODED VIEW. Separate only four logical groups by modest distances and dashed assembly lines: upper protective armor, central sensor/chassis core, outrigger/claw mechanisms, twin compact maneuver modules and belly capture saddle. Underneath show the SAME machine in deployed and folded service states. The black sensor-face band must remain IDENTIFIABLE in both; if partly protected during folding, show the actual protective shutter and a simple motion arrow, not an unexplained new face. Arms fold toward the same chassis; no missing or extra appendages.
RIGHT HARVESTER: show the SAME low heavy work core, EXACTLY FOUR main working arms (two thick anchoring clamp arms, two secondary tool arms with cutter and gripper), small rear stabilizing legs, removable rear ore cassette. Explode the upper armor and ore cassette upward and tool tips outward, keep all arm roots attached to the central structural chassis. Show one detailed detachable tool-head mount with paired clamps, retained connector and a load path, plus a small cassette exchange sketch showing one empty dock and the SAME cassette moving along guide rails. Do not double the number of arms or make the ore bin a separate spaceship.
Across bottom center: a shared original rectangular capture saddle, paired locking lugs, tow attachment and covered service port, repeated on both machines in matching relative belly locations. Keep assembly lines clean, no dimension claims, no exact manufacturing specs, no tiny paragraphs. Labels only EXPLORER / HARVESTER / DEPLOYED / STOWED / TOOL INTERFACE / SHARED CAPTURE. Show real mechanical relationships at concept level, not decorative floating parts.

The STERN correctly defines SIX main nozzles as TWO horizontal banks, each with THREE vertically stacked nozzles. The other two nozzles in each vertical stack are hidden directly underneath/above in projection. Do not draw a third central main nozzle. Use case: precise-object-edit. Image 1 is the exploded/cutaway target. Image 2 is the authoritative exterior master of the SAME GUIHANG ship. Keep the upper exploded main ship and the overall page, design language, coloring and zones. Correct these exact inconsistencies:
1. LOWER longitudinal cutaway currently shows THREE open hangar rooms. Rebuild that LOCAL midship region to show exactly TWO port-side working openings and ONE thick pier in between, at the same longitudinal positions as image 2. Do NOT merely close the last opening: the current two forward rooms are wrongly packed too far forward. The FORWARD launch opening must span roughly the 28–41 percent section of ship length and the AFT recovery opening roughly 44–64 percent, visually aligned to the reference; percentages are instructions, NOT numbers to draw. Reorganize internal equipment to fit those two bays. Do not put a new third bay under INDUSTRY.
2. The protected rotating-habitat candidate is behind/inboard of those two bays, and upper occupied decks may be visible above them, but the HANGAR label must bracket BOTH existing side bays and HABITAT should use a leader to the inner/upper habitation volume. Keep SHIELD, PRESERVATION, INDUSTRY, POWER, DRIVE labels with their actual regions. Don't add exterior rings.
3. In UPPER exploded view, the text ENGINE ASSEMBLY (6 NOZZLES) currently points to an ordinary detached armor panel. Move its leader clearly to the assembled aft nozzle cluster; the detached plate is just armor, not a propulsion unit. Keep six nozzle total and all key exterior identity.
4. Do not present the detached flat side cladding as though it itself contains working doors; caption it PORT SERVICE ARMOR. The underlying paired bay structure stays connected to the spine.
Preserve clear hand-drawn ink and restrained marker on ivory paper, exact original ship identity, no new styles or dimension claims. Fix the diagram, not merely its prose.

Use case: stylized-concept. Draw a focused HAND-DRAWN PORT MECHANISM and TRANSFER concept sheet for the SAME GUIHANG twin side hangars in images 1 and 2, machines from image 3. Ivory paper, pencil/ink construction lines, warm-white/blue-gray/graphite and sparse brick-red, quiet marker shading. Landscape 1536x1024. This is explanatory concept design, not actual engineering certification.
Top half: THREE matching side-section panels of ONE MACHINE TRANSIT DOOR: CLOSED / LIFTING / OPEN. Commit to a clear ORIGINAL design refinement: one reinforced door leaf lifts VERTICALLY into a tall protected pocket directly ABOVE the same opening, guided by rails on both jambs. Show the complete pocket height and upper closed end, actual leaf remains INSIDE hull structure in the OPEN panel, never floating above hull. Door down blocks opening in CLOSED, halfway up in LIFTING, completely clear of the same vehicle transit opening in OPEN. One clean upward arrow for motion. Keep leaf thickness, opening dimensions and hardware consistent across the three panels. An amber interlock and fixed inner capture rail are present; leaf motion must not pass through the captured machine.
Bottom left 55 percent: legible TOP-DOWN floor/rail diagram of the SAME two independent side-facing lanes. Exterior space to LEFT; launch upper lane arrow outward LEFT; recovery lower lane arrow inward RIGHT. Both lanes end at one shared TRANSFER SHUTTLE track running vertically along their inboard ends. A mobile carriage on that cross-track transfers a LOCKED machine cradle between lane and maintenance berth; draw rails and carriage explicitly, not rail segments ending in empty space. Two clear HOLD marks ensure one machine movement at a time through shared transfer, not simultaneous crossing. Add dedicated UNLOAD pocket beside recovery and ISOLATION/REPAIR pocket beyond it, separated from the outgoing lane. Minimal labels LAUNCH / RECOVERY / TRANSFER / HOLD / UNLOAD / ISOLATION.
Bottom right: one perspective mechanical detail of the transfer carriage with a neutral folded machine locked on top, visible clamps, cross-rail wheels/guides and service connector still disconnected until fixation. Tiny suited human tethered nearby provides approximate scale only; no exact sizes.
Keep the two exterior ports and central structural pier consistent with prior sheets. The pressure boundary is the small service boxes, not the entire vacuum working hangar. NO mecha battle, no three exterior doors, no dimensions, no unrelated hull redesign or decorative background.

content.prompt: Use case: precise-object-edit. Edit ONLY the small circular HABITAT SECTION diagram at bottom center of this concept sheet. Preserve the large common-room perspective, bottom-left floor plan, bottom-right table exploded detail, color, ink/marker style and all other content. The orange COMMON ROOM sector is currently on the right of the ring, while its people stand vertically: this contradicts radial outward gravity. Move the orange common room sector to the SIX O'CLOCK BOTTOM part of the circular habitat drum. Draw its people standing on the OUTER bottom arc floor, FEET DOWN toward the ring's exterior and HEADS UP toward its center. Place a single radial OUTWARD (ARTIFICIAL GRAVITY) arrow straight down from this bottom room toward the outside of the ring, avoiding people. Relocate COMMON ROOM (INSIDE DRUM) leader to this bottom orange sector. Keep non-rotating outer hull and service spine, rotating habitat drum identities clear, remove the old orange room on the right. All large interior design and page layout remain unchanged. This is a hand-drawn concept section, not an engineering approval.

Use case: precise-object-edit. Edit this original SENTINEL mechanical concept sheet to fix two specific review findings. Preserve the whole FRONT figure, colors, silhouette, left-arm shield/right-hand carbine, backpack identity and paper/ink style. 1) In the center BACK view, preserve the upper back with two rectangular propulsion pods, middle docking saddle and service socket. REDRAW THE LOWER HALF AS A TRUE REAR VIEW: rear pelvis plates, back-of-knee actuators, calf rear panels with maintenance slots, ankle back/heel housings facing the viewer. The wide feet point AWAY from the viewer; show heel faces, not the front toe segments. No front groin armor or front shin plates in BACK. Shield stays on machine left (image left in back view) and carbine stays on machine right (image right in back view); do not mirror entire figure. 2) In bottom-right CAPTURE INTERFACE detail, numbers above the two central upright saddle lugs currently incorrectly reuse 1 and 2. Rename these lug callouts '3a' and '3b'. Keep 3 the central docking saddle and 4 the service connector; main back and exploded labels 1 and 2 continue to identify propulsion pods. These are localized corrections; preserve other content and readable compact labels.

Use case: precise-object-edit.
